Welcome. I’m really glad you’re here with me, because together, we’re about to step into a world most folks only glimpse from a distance—the world of low-wage work in America.
Imagine putting your heart and soul into a job, showing up every day with determination, only to find that the finish line keeps moving just out of reach. That’s the daily reality for millions. It’s a place where hard work and grit often run headfirst into obstacles that seem impossible to overcome.
In her eye-opening book, Nickel and Dimed: On (Not) Getting By in America, Barbara Ehrenreich takes us on an unforgettable journey. She doesn’t just report from the sidelines—she rolls up her sleeves and walks in the shoes of those who clean hotel rooms, serve up food in diners, and stock the shelves at big-box stores. Through her experiences, we get an honest, unfiltered look at the struggle to find dignity, security, and a sense of self-worth, all while living under the constant pressure of making ends meet.
As we move through bustling kitchens, watch paychecks disappear into rent and groceries, and feel the toll these jobs take on both body and spirit, we’re invited to rethink what we believe about opportunity and the American dream. Are hard work and perseverance really enough? What does it actually take to get by?
We’ll discover moments of connection, frustration, and hope—and see how resilience grows, even in the toughest of circumstances. Together, let’s pull back the curtain and explore the invisible challenges and quiet victories that shape the lives of America’s working poor. There’s so much to uncover, and it just might change the way we see the world around us.
